authors: One An, Marcus J. Min, Xujie Si and Osbert Bastani (building on ProofNet by Azerbayev et al. and ProofNet# by Poiroux et al.)
title: ProofNet-Verified, explained
h1: ProofNet-Verified: 367 textbook exercises, re-checked for what they really say
lead: ProofNet-Verified is a benchmark, not a proof library: 367 undergraduate exercises, each stated in Lean with its proof deliberately left as sorry for an AI prover to fill in. Its contribution is an audit of the older ProofNet statements: in 205 of 367 (55.9%) the formal statement did not say what the exercise says (often it was outright false), and every one was corrected.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of ProofNet-Verified, an audited and corrected version of the ProofNet theorem-proving benchmark: what its 367 Lean problem statements are, how six of them went wrong in the original, and how the Lean side is checked.
startNote: Every Lean file here is one exercise whose proof is sorry on purpose: the benchmark is for provers to solve. Start with a typical problem, then read the five error stories: a missing n > 0, a missing pair of brackets, a sign convention, a statement about types instead of numbers and the wrong group (the one file that ships a full proof). The ten textbook nodes summarise the rest.
sizeNote: 367 Lean problem files (about 6,150 lines), one theorem each, almost all ending in sorry by design; plus archived and original copies, Python scripts and JSON audit records.
agentCtx: ProofNet-Verified: an audited/corrected Lean 4 version of the ProofNet autoformalization and theorem-proving benchmark. 367 single-theorem files (proofnet-verified-latest/proofnet-N.lean), proofs left as sorry; error taxonomy JSON compares them with the original ProofNet and ProofNet# statements.

gloss.Group: A group: a set with an associative multiplication, an identity and inverses.
gloss.Field: A field: a commutative ring in which every non-zero element has an inverse (ℚ, ℝ, ℂ, 𝔽ₚ).
gloss.Prime: Mathlib's general notion of a prime element; for natural numbers it means the usual primes.
gloss.Irreducible: Not a unit, and in every factorisation a·b one of the factors is a unit. For polynomials over a field: non-constant and not a product of two non-constant polynomials.
gloss.Polynomial: Polynomial R is R[x], polynomials with coefficients in R; X is the variable.
gloss.IsEmpty: IsEmpty α: the type α has no elements. Used here to say there is no isomorphism.
gloss.BddBelow: A set of reals is bounded below: some number is ≤ every element.
gloss.InnerProductSpace: A vector space with an inner product ⟨u, v⟩. Mathlib's is conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in the second.
gloss.NormedAddCommGroup: An additive group with a norm ‖·‖; the setting for inner-product spaces in Mathlib.
gloss.FiniteDimensional: The vector space has a finite basis.
gloss.AddCommGroup: An abelian group written additively; the vectors of a vector space form one.
gloss.Module: Module F V: V is a vector space over F (Mathlib's word for vector spaces over any ring).
gloss.End: End F V: linear maps from V to itself; * on them is composition.
gloss.closure: Subgroup.closure S: the subgroup generated by the set S.
gloss.eigenspace: eigenspace T c: the vectors v with T v = c·v (always contains 0).
gloss.finrank: The dimension of a finite-dimensional vector space.
gloss.card: Fintype.card α: the number of elements of a finite type.
gloss.sInf: The infimum of a set of reals (with a junk value 0 when it has none).
gloss.sSup: The supremum of a set of reals (with a junk value 0 when it has none).
gloss.Set: Set α: a set of elements of α.
